claim: The General Assembly meets in organizational session on the second Tuesday in January after the House election
quote: The General Assembly shall meet in organizational session on the second Tuesday in January next succeeding the election of the members of the House of Representatives

claim: The organizational session lasts no more than 15 days and passes no legislation; the regular session follows
quote: The General Assembly shall remain in session for organizational purposes not longer than fifteen consecutive calendar days, during which session no legislation shall be passed on third and final consideration

claim: The governor has ten days, Sundays excepted, to act on a bill or it becomes law
quote: within ten calendar days (Sundays excepted) after it shall have been presented to him, the same shall become a law without his signature

claim: After adjournment, a bill becomes law unless the governor files a veto within the ten-day period
quote: If the General Assembly by its adjournment prevents the return of any bill within said ten-day period, the bill shall become a law, unless disapproved by the Governor

claim: General laws take effect 40 days after passage unless the act says the public welfare requires sooner
quote: No law of a general nature shall take effect until forty days after its passage unless the same or the caption thereof shall state that the public welfare requires that it should take effect sooner.

claim: Local (private) acts are void unless approved by two-thirds of the local legislative body or by local referendum
quote: shall be void and of no effect unless the act by its terms either requires the approval by a two-thirds vote of the local legislative body of the municipality or county

claim: The regular August election is the first Thursday in August of every even-numbered year
quote: means the election held on the first Thursday in August of every even-numbered year

claim: The regular November election is the Tuesday after the first Monday in November of every even-numbered year
quote: means the election held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November in every even-numbered year

claim: County offices, constables, judges and the county legislative body are elected at the regular August election
quote: Elections for the following offices shall be held at the regular August election when the election immediately precedes the commencement of a full term

claim: Judicial and other civil officers are elected on the first Thursday in August before their terms expire, with terms starting 1 September
quote: on the first Thursday in August next preceding the expiration of their respective terms of service

claim: County primaries for August offices are held on the first Tuesday in May
quote: shall be held on the first Tuesday in May before the August election

claim: In presidential years a party may hold its county primary on the presidential preference primary day
quote: a political party primary for offices to be elected in the regular August election may be held on the same day as the presidential preference primary

claim: Statewide parties must nominate by primary for offices elected on a partisan basis at the August or November election
quote: statewide political parties shall nominate their candidates in primary elections for all offices for which partisan elections are held at the regular August or regular November election

claim: Since 2025, a county party that nominated by another method in 2022 or 2024 may keep doing so (except for governor, legislature and Congress)
quote: nominated a candidate by a method other than a primary election for elections held in 2022 or 2024

claim: Parties may nominate for offices outside the required list by party rules or by primary
quote: by any method authorized under the rules of the party or by primary election under this title

claim: A county party that chooses a primary must tell the county election commission in writing at least 180 days before qualifying
quote: the county executive committee shall, at least one hundred eighty (180) days before the qualifying deadline, direct, in writing, the county election commission

claim: Only a statewide or recognized minor party nominee may carry a party label for a county office
quote: or for any office to be voted on by the voters of a county, unless the political party

claim: Voters do not register by party; a voter may vote in a primary by declaring allegiance to the party and intent to affiliate
quote: the voter declares allegiance to the political party in whose primary the voter seeks to vote and states that the voter intends to affiliate with that party

claim: Voting in a party primary without being a bona fide member or without intent to affiliate is a crime
quote: if a person votes in a political party's primary without being a bona fide member of or affiliated with that political party

claim: Municipal elections are nonpartisan
quote: municipal elections shall be nonpartisan

claim: A city charter may allow partisan elections, in which case parties may nominate
quote: unless the municipality's charter specifically permits partisan elections

claim: In a metropolitan government, the mayor and metro council elections count as municipal (nonpartisan) elections
quote: the election of the county mayor and the members of the legislative body of such metropolitan government shall be considered to be municipal elections within the meaning of this section

claim: Cities under the modified city manager-council charter hold only nonpartisan elections
quote: All elections shall be nonpartisan.

claim: Metropolitan counties still hold county primary elections
quote: All counties in the state which have a metropolitan form of government shall bear the expense of holding county primary elections

claim: In a county over 825,000 people, the county legislative body may make trial court and county judicial elections nonpartisan by two-thirds vote
quote: may require that all elections to fill state trial court judgeships and county judicial offices in such county shall be conducted in a nonpartisan manner

claim: School board elections may be partisan or nonpartisan
quote: Elections for school board members may be conducted on a partisan or nonpartisan basis.

claim: If one county primary board of a party opts for partisan school board elections, candidates on any board in that county may run as party nominees
quote: If at least one (1) county primary board of a political party elects to conduct school board elections on a partisan basis

claim: School board members serve four-year terms
quote: The members of the board shall be elected for a term of four (4) years, and may succeed themselves.

claim: County school board members are elected from districts of substantially equal population
quote: Members of county boards of education shall be residents of and elected from districts of substantially equal population

claim: Special school district boards are elected as their private act provides, on staggered terms
quote: Members of special school district boards of education shall be elected according to special or private act

claim: Municipal school boards may be elected the same way as the city's governing body
quote: members of municipal boards of education may be elected in the same manner, either from districts or at large, or a combination of both

claim: No new special school districts may be created after April 30, 1982
quote: No additional special school districts may be created after April 30, 1982

claim: In a primary the candidate with the most votes is nominated; there is no runoff
quote: The candidates who receive the highest number of votes shall be declared elected or nominated

claim: On a tie for a county or city office, the county or municipal legislative body breaks it or calls a runoff
quote: the legislative body may by resolution call for a run-off election between the tied candidates

claim: Runoffs exist only where a city charter provides for them
quote: in any municipality in which the charter of such municipality provides for a runoff election following a primary election for municipal office

claim: Ranked choice and instant runoff voting are banned for state and local offices
quote: A county election commission shall not utilize instant runoff voting or ranked choice voting

claim: Candidates not nominated by a party are called independent candidates
quote: Candidates who are not to be placed on ballots as nominees of a political party shall be known as

claim: Independent candidates qualify by nominating petition signed by registered voters eligible to vote for that office
quote: registered voters who are eligible to vote to fill the office

claim: Independents for offices on the county primary ballot file when primary candidates file
quote: Independent candidates for offices which will appear on the county primary ballot shall qualify by filing their petitions at the same time primary candidates qualify.

claim: City candidates file their petition with the county election commission where the city is located
quote: Each candidate for municipal office shall file the candidate's original nominating petition with the county election commission where the municipality is located.

claim: Tennessee has 95 counties, listed in statute
quote: The state is divided into the following counties:

claim: Each county elects a legislative body, county executive, sheriff, trustee, register, county clerk and assessor of property for four-year terms
quote: The qualified voters of each county shall elect for terms of four years a legislative body, a county executive, a Sheriff, a Trustee, a Register, a County Clerk and an Assessor of Property.

claim: The county legislative body has at most 25 members, no more than three per district, reapportioned every ten years
quote: The legislative body shall not exceed twenty-five members, and no more than three representatives shall be elected from a district.

claim: A consolidated (metropolitan) county is exempt from having the standard county executive and legislative body
quote: shall be exempt from having a county executive and a county legislative body as described in this paragraph

claim: The General Assembly may provide alternate forms of county government, including charters, adopted by referendum
quote: The General Assembly may provide alternate forms of county government including the right to charter

claim: The county legislative body has 9 to 25 members
quote: shall be composed of not less than nine (9) nor more than twenty-five (25) members

claim: Members are called county commissioners and collectively the board of county commissioners
quote: The members of the county legislative body shall be known individually as county commissioners and collectively as the board of county commissioners.

claim: Commissioners serve four-year terms, all elected at the same August election every four years
quote: Members of the county legislative body shall be elected in the regular August election in 1978 and every four (4) years thereafter.

claim: The old quarterly county court and other county legislative forms were abolished in 1978
quote: the quarterly county court, county council and any other forms of county legislative bodies are abolished

claim: Outside metropolitan counties, the county's chief executive is a county mayor elected for four years
quote: the chief executive officer of each county shall be a county mayor elected

claim: Counties that titled the office county executive by private act before 28 March 2007 may keep that title
quote: Private acts enacted prior to March 28, 2007, designating the title of the chief executive officer of the county as

claim: The county mayor is elected at the August election every four years on the 1978 cycle
quote: the county mayor shall be elected in the regular August election in 1978 and every four (4) years thereafter

claim: Each county elects a trustee for four years
quote: A county trustee is elected for each county by the qualified voters thereof, and holds office for four (4) years

claim: Each county elects a register for four years
quote: A register is elected for each county by the qualified voters thereof

claim: Constables are elected by civil district: two in the district with the county seat, one in each other district, for two years
quote: Two (2) constables shall be elected by the qualified voters in the civil district of each county which includes the county town, and one (1) in every other civil district of the county

claim: A county legislative body may abolish constables or set a two- or four-year term by two-thirds vote at two meetings
quote: abolish the office of constable for that county or set the term of office for the constable at either two (2) or four (4) years

claim: A county may create a coroner office, filled by the county legislative body, not by voters
quote: If such office is created, the county legislative body shall elect a coroner

claim: Any county may adopt a charter by referendum
quote: Each county in this state may adopt a charter form of government as provided in this part.

claim: A county charter sets the size and method of election of the county legislative body
quote: For the size, method of election, qualification for holding office, method of removal, and procedures of the county legislative body

claim: A charter cannot reduce the duties of the sheriff, register, county clerk, assessor or trustee
quote: may be interpreted or amended to alter, amend, or reduce the duties, qualifications, or privileges of the charter or constitutional county offices of sheriff, register, county clerk, assessor of property, or trustee

claim: A metropolitan government is the consolidation of a county and its city or cities
quote: means the political entity created by consolidation of all, or substantially all, of the political and corporate functions of a county and a city or cities

claim: City-county consolidation needs a majority inside the city and a majority in the county outside it
quote: approved by a majority of those voting within the municipal corporation and by a majority of those voting in the county outside the municipal corporation

claim: A metropolitan government covers the whole county
quote: That the territory embraced in the metropolitan government shall be the total area of the county

claim: A metropolitan government has a general services district and an urban services district
quote: a general services district and an urban services district

claim: Smaller cities may be excluded from the metro and keep their own government
quote: Any smaller city that has been excluded from a metropolitan government

claim: Under the mayor-aldermanic charter the board is the mayor and aldermen
quote: means the mayor and the aldermen

claim: A small mayor-aldermanic town incorporated after June 1991 starts with a mayor and two aldermen at large
quote: its board shall consist of a mayor and two (2) aldermen elected at large

claim: Mayor-aldermanic officers serve four-year terms after the first election
quote: At each election thereafter the mayor and aldermen shall be elected to four-year terms

claim: An older mayor-aldermanic town may set its aldermen between two and eight by ordinance
quote: increase or decrease the number of aldermen to no fewer than two (2) and no more than eight (8)

claim: A city manager-commission city of 5,000 or more starts with five commissioners
quote: there shall be elected at the first election five (5) commissioners

claim: Commissioners in a city manager-commission city serve four-year terms
quote: The term of all commissioners thereafter elected shall be for four (4) years

claim: A city manager-commission board fixes its own election dates
quote: The board of commissioners shall fix the date of all subsequent elections

claim: Incorporating under the city manager-commission charter needs at least 1,500 residents
quote: No unincorporated territory shall be incorporated under chapters 18-22 of this title unless such territory contains not less than one thousand five hundred (1,500) persons

claim: Incorporating under the modified city manager-council charter needs at least 5,000 residents
quote: unless such territory contains not less than five thousand (5,000) persons, who shall be actual residents of the territory

claim: Under the modified city manager-council charter, one council member is elected from each voting precinct
quote: One (1) member of the council shall be elected from each voting precinct of the incorporated area

claim: Modified city manager-council cities hold a regular municipal election every two years
quote: a regular municipal election shall be held biennially thereafter

claim: Modified city manager-council members serve four-year terms
quote: The terms of council members elected at this and all succeeding elections for the office of council shall be four (4) years.

claim: Any city, even one chartered by private act, may move its elections to the August or November general election by ordinance
quote: Notwithstanding any private act of a municipality to the contrary, the legislative body of a municipality may by ordinance change the date of municipal elections to coincide with the August or November general election.

claim: Terms may be extended no more than two years to make the move
quote: but no term may be extended for more than two (2) years beyond its regular expiration date

claim: A city that moved its election date may move it back once
quote: The board may only make an election date change under this subsection (c) one (1) time.

claim: The county election commission runs city elections; a city in several counties is run by the county with its city hall
quote: shall be called and conducted by the county election commission of the county in which the town seat or city hall is located

claim: City councils and elected school boards may not use nominate-by-district, elect-at-large systems
quote: shall be elected to such office through an election procedure requiring candidates to be nominated from a district and elected at-large

claim: A city adopts home rule by ordinance and a majority vote of its voters
quote: Any municipality may by ordinance submit to its qualified voters in a general or special election the question

claim: The General Assembly may act on a home rule city only by general law
quote: the General Assembly shall act with respect to such home rule municipality only by laws which are general in terms and effect

claim: A home rule charter provision is void if it conflicts with a general act (pay excepted)
quote: no charter provision except with respect to compensation of municipal personnel shall be effective if inconsistent with any general act of the General Assembly

claim: A home rule city's council may propose charter amendments by ordinance for voter approval
quote: the local governing body of any municipality that has adopted home rule may, by ordinance, propose an amendment to the charter of such municipality by a majority vote of the body

claim: Tennessee's three metropolitan governments are Nashville-Davidson, Lynchburg-Moore and Hartsville-Trousdale
quote: only Nashville-Davidson County, Lynchburg-Moore County and Hartsville-Trousdale County have adopted a consolidated form of government

claim: Shelby and Knox are the only charter counties
quote: To date, only Shelby and Knox counties have chosen county charters
